EXECUTION_POLICIES:
**Milestone steps**: Plan steps are checkpoints the execute-phase agent owns end-to-end; it may use reasoning and local todos inside a step. Each ``description`` states the milestone only—fewer than 20 words—not a full procedure or tool script.
**Granularity**: - First plan-generate (```` execute iteration 1, no execute evidence in ledger): **1–2 steps only** — never 3+ - Later plan-generate calls (execute iteration 2+): 1–3 steps per decision - Each step has a checkable ``expected_output`` - Step ``id``: short local tokens (e.g. ``01``, ``02``, or next free per ````). ``dependencies`` must reference those same ``id`` strings (runtime may normalize numeric spelling; prefer exact matches). - ``description``: imperative outcome/scope line, not the raw goal string - Merge related filesystem reads into one step when they are sequential tool-only work - ``parallel``: independent readonly steps only, with descriptions naming disjoint scopes (e.g. separate explore targets)
**Progress-aware** (use assess ``Progress`` when present): ``high`` → favor 1–2 closing or verify steps. On the **first** plan-generate, stay within the 1–2 step hard cap even when Progress is ``none`` / ``low`` / ``medium`` (bundle recon into one explore milestone rather than many steps). On later iterations, stage within the 1–3 cap.
**Filesystem discovery**: - Do not fan out many parallel shallow ``list_files`` / ``glob`` calls on overlapping paths; prefer one reconnaissance step then sequential targeted ``read_file`` / ``grep``. - Use ``parallel`` execution_mode only when steps are readonly and name **disjoint** subtrees or files; avoid parallel “scan the whole repo” patterns. - ``glob`` can be expensive on large workspaces—use narrow patterns and depth limits when possible.
**Readonly discovery plans**: - When the next work is mostly **readonly** discovery (search, skim files, map structure), prefer concise targeted steps over broad repository-wide scans. - Split into multiple discovery steps only when scopes are genuinely disjoint.
**First-wave constraint** (overrides general granularity on the first plan-generate): - When ```` shows execute iteration **1** and the ledger has no execute-step tool/subagent results: emit **1–2 steps only** (never 3+). Runtime truncates extras. - Rationale: validate direction before committing to a long DAG; catch wrong approaches early.
**Step consolidation**: Merge sequential reads of related files or single-topic discovery+analysis into one milestone when they are not independent parallel work. Split only for true parallelism or different subagent needs.
